biodiversity_overview.text: 3,319 GBIF occurrence records for 53 tracked species are attributed to Bihar, spanning 1898-2026.
3,216 of these records (96.9%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 23, Magnoliopsida 9, Mammalia 9, Testudines 5, Squamata 3, Actinopterygii 2, Amphibia 1, Crocodylia 1.

threatened_species.text: 6 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Tiger (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU), Asian Elephant (EN), Indian Rhinoceros (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Pied Starling (845), Indian Roller (487), Indian Pond-heron (258), Indian Golden Oriole (238), Indian Grey-Hornbill (203).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 31 in 2016 to 71 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 4.13% of Bihar's area (16 areas intersect the state).
6.6% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (211 of 3,216); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Peacock Soft-shelled Turtle (0.50), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Courser (0.47), Mugger Crocodile (0.46).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Bihar (equal-weight reference): cell near 25.875N 85.875E (overall rank 146, median rank across weightings 166); cell near 25.875N 85.125E (overall rank 182, median rank across weightings 203); cell near 25.125N 87.375E (overall rank 188, median rank across weightings 202).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 1,867 km2 (1.98% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

19.4 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (1.04% of the 2000 extent; 0.14% in 2015-2024, rank 25 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2009 (3.83 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 2.31% of land and population density is 1,348.8 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
34% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
